history.period: disputed: estimates range from 10th-11th century to 16th-20th century
history.summary: Ancient Durga temple at Diuri village, Tamar block, about 60 km from Ranchi on the Ranchi-Tata road (NH-33). Its distinction is the 16-armed (solahbhuji) stone idol of the goddess, about 3 feet tall, claimed locally to be the only 16-armed Durga idol worshipped in the country. The temple is built of large interlocking sandstone blocks without cementing material; before it stood, the goddess was worshipped in a sacred grove (sarna). Worship is shared: tribal Munda Pahan priests perform puja on six days and a Brahmin panda on one. Legend credits Adivasi king Kera (c. 1300) with building the temple after the goddess restored his lost kingdom; another legend has a Tamar king rediscovering it after a dream. The district administration took over management in October 2020. MS Dhoni is a noted devotee. (verify) The brief's claims of a '16 temples complex' and a 'Lord Rama legend' found no support in consulted sources and are not included. Dating is unsettled: one directory says 10th-11th century, Wikipedia says the present structure dates between the 16th and 20th centuries, and local tradition says 700 years old. CSV town 'Ranchi' corrected to Tamar (actual village: Diuri).

name: Deori Mandir
town_description: Tamar is a town and block headquarters in Ranchi district, Jharkhand, on the Ranchi-Tata highway (NH-33), about 60 km from Ranchi. The temple stands in Diuri village within Tamar block.

travel.road: On the right side of the Ranchi-Tata road (NH-33) toward Tamar; Diuri village is on the highway
